deep.reconstruction:
Problem: find the Euler buckling load of a column of height a whose flexural rigidity varies along its length. Euler writes the rigidity as EI(x) = (α + βx/a)^{4λ}·Ekk. Put s = α + βx/a. The deflection equation EI·y'' + P·y = 0 becomes d²y/ds² + n² s^{-4λ} y = 0, with P = n²β²Ekk/a². The page belongs to the family of exponents for which this is elementary (Bessel order ν = 1/(2−4λ) a half-integer, or the Euler-equation case).

Case on this page: exponent 4/3 (λ = 1/3). The solution is √s·Z_{3/2}(3n s^{1/3}), i.e. a sine/cosine of 3n s^{1/3} with a correction term 1/(3n s^{1/3}). The end conditions give the transcendental eigen-condition from the previous page:
3n∛α + arctan(1/(3n∛α)) − 3n∛(α+β) − arctan(1/(3n∛(α+β))) = π.

Art. XXIX makes two approximations:
(i) For β ≪ α, n is large, so each arctan is replaced by its argument.
(ii) Dropping the O(1/n) terms gives n ≈ −π/(3[∛(α+β) − ∛α]), hence P ≈ π²β²/(9[∛(α+β) − ∛α]²)·Ekk/a².

Euler claims the error stays small as long as β is not much larger than α, and tests β = α:
- the approximation gives |n| = π/(3(2^{1/3} − 1)) = 4.0289/∛α;
- solving the exact condition gives 4.0505/∛α, so P = 16.4065·α∛α·Ekk/a².

For α = 1 (rigidity rising from Ekk to 2^{4/3}Ekk) this gives P = 16.4065 Ekk/a². He compares two other cases:
- rigidity (1 + x/a)^4 gives P = 39.47844 Ekk/a² = 4π²;
- constant rigidity gives P = π² = 9.86961 Ekk/a².

Art. XXX then opens the case exponent 8/3 (λ = 2/3), worked on the next page.

Modern reading: the approximation in (ii) is exactly the leading Liouville–Green (WKB) eigenvalue estimate, P ≈ π²/(∫₀^a dx/√EI)². Here ∫ s^{-2/3} ds = 3s^{1/3}. The same structure reappears in the 8/3 formula on the next page, and the estimate is exact in the exponent-4 case, where P = π²·√(EI_C·EI_A)/a².
errors: Minor rounding: π² = 9.869604…, so 9.86960 rather than 9.86961; 4π² = 39.478418, so 39.47842 rather than 39.47844.
My recomputation of the β = α root gives |n| ≈ 4.0506 (P ≈ 16.407), consistent with Euler's 4.0505 / 16.4065 to about 4–5 significant figures; essentially correct.
Sign convention: n comes out negative, which is harmless since only n² enters P.
Article numbering: 'XXX' is used here for Example 3 and again on the next page for Example 4; the second should presumably be XXXI.
On the previous page, 'A tg 2/(3n∛(α+β))' should read 1/(3n∛(α+β)), as the formula on this page confirms.

ideas.what: Buckling load of a column with power-law variable rigidity (α + βx/a)^m, solved in closed form for special exponents (4/3, 8/3, 4, 2)
ideas.modern_name: Buckling of tapered / non-uniform columns; half-integer-order Bessel (spherical Bessel) solutions and the Euler–Cauchy equation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (E238) for the first treatment; later systematic Bessel-function treatment by Dinnik and others in the early 20th century
ideas.where_published: E238 itself; discussed in Truesdell's history of elastic bodies (Opera omnia II.11/2)

ideas.what: Approximation of the eigenvalue by the phase integral 3n[∛(α+β) − ∛α] = π, i.e. P ≈ π²/(∫dx/√EI)²
ideas.where_published: Only as these special-case formulas in E238; no general statement known to me

ideas.what: Numerical solution of the transcendental eigen-condition for β = α, checking the accuracy of the approximation (about 0.5% in n, 1% in P)
ideas.modern_name: Root-finding for a characteristic equation and error assessment of an asymptotic formula

ideas.what: Exact result for rigidity ∝ s^4: P = 4π² Ekk/a² for doubling of s, i.e. P = π²√(EI_C·EI_A)/a²
ideas.modern_name: Closed-form buckling load for the s^4 rigidity law (WKB exact)

missed.claim: Euler's approximate buckling formulas for the variable-rigidity column (exponents 4/3 and 8/3) are exactly the leading-order Liouville–Green/WKB eigenvalue estimate P ≈ π²/(∫₀^a dx/√EI)². The estimate is exact for the exponent-4 law, and Euler numerically assesses its accuracy. He thus has, in special cases, the phase-integral approximation about 80 years before Liouville and Green, though he never states it as a general rule.
missed.quote: les arcs seront à peu près égaux à leur tangentes … d'où nous tirons assez près n = −π/(3∛(α+β) − 3∛α)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historical precedent for WKB-type eigenvalue estimates in structural stability. Engineering texts give the 'equivalent-rigidity' formula P ≈ π²/(∫dx/√EI)² without attributing it to Euler.

deep.surprise_reason: The computations are known content of E238, and Truesdell discusses the variable-section column. Seeing Euler's approximation as a Liouville–Green phase-integral estimate, exact for the s^4 case, is a mild connection I have not seen stated explicitly in the literature.
transcription_corrections: Art. XXX: the rigidity law reads (α + βx/a)^{8/3}·Ekk; the small mark over α in the scan appears to be an artifact, not an exponent.
The machine 'α^{1/?}' and '[?]' in Art. XXX should be removed.
Previous page: 'A tg 2/(3n∛(α+β))' should be 'A tg 1/(3n∛(α+β))'.
